privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lastUpdated: Last updated 18 September 2026. This page is a working draft for the first public site. It has not received legal review and is not legal advice.

sections.heading: Who we are
paragraphs: This website is published by {legalName}, a founder-led digital product company. You can contact us at {email}.

sections.heading: What this site collects
paragraphs: The public pages do not use advertising trackers, analytics cookies or unnecessary cookies. We do not implement Google Analytics.

If you send a message through the contact form or email, we receive the name, email address, organisation (if you provide one) and message that you submit, so that we can reply. We do not sell this information.

sections.heading: Cookies
paragraphs: This version of the site does not set advertising or analytics cookies. Hosting providers such as Vercel may process technical logs (for example IP address, browser and request time) to operate and secure the service. If we later add privacy-conscious analytics, this page will be updated before those tools are switched on.

sections.heading: Where messages go
paragraphs: If a contact form endpoint is configured, submissions are posted to that provider so we can read them. If no endpoint is configured, the form opens your email application addressed to {email}. Do not send passwords, payment details or confidential third-party material through this form.

sections.heading: How long we keep it
paragraphs: Enquiry messages are kept for as long as needed to respond and to maintain a record of the conversation, then deleted unless we have a continuing reason to hold them (for example an active project discussion).

sections.heading: Your rights
paragraphs: If you are in the UK or EEA you may have rights to access, correct or delete personal data we hold about you, and to object to or restrict certain processing. Email {email} to ask. You may also complain to the Information Commissioner’s Office.

sections.heading: Changes
paragraphs: We will update this page if the way the site handles information changes. The date at the top will change when we do.

sections.headline: Digital products people come back for.
sections.supporting: We build for sport, media and the screen. Strong ideas, turned into things you can play, watch and return to — with a bit of Saturday in them.

sections.heading: Made to be opened again.
paragraphs: Player29 is a founder-led company that shapes and builds digital products for sport, media and the screen.
We get excited about the moment a product earns another look: a decision that actually matters, a match that could go either way, a reason to come back with your mates.

sections.description: A compact football management game built around the calls that change a match — then replay it, argue about it, and play it with friends.

frame.footerCopy: One call that swings the match. Not a to-do list in a kit.

sections.heading: How we help an idea live.

items.title: Find the product
items.copy: Who it is for, why it should exist, and what would make someone come back. We get that straight while the idea is still exciting — not after it has been flattened into a plan.

items.title: Make it real
items.copy: We design and build focused applications: clear to use, good to look at, and honest about what they are. A first version you can put in someone’s hands.

items.title: Mobile and Beyond
items.copy: Phones first, then wherever the audience already is. We care about how it feels in the hand, on a bigger screen, and in the five minutes before something kicks off.

items.title: Bring IP to life
items.copy: A brand, a format, a set of rules people already love. We turn that into a digital product without sanding off what made it special.

sections.intro: The products people return to start with a simple question: what has to be true for this to matter?

stages.title: Get under the skin of it
stages.copy: Who it is for, why now, and what would make it feel like a fixture in their week.

stages.title: Shape something you can feel
stages.copy: The few things that matter, a path through the product, and an interface we can actually build.

stages.title: Put it in people’s hands
stages.copy: A focused first slice, out in the world. Then we watch what people do — not what they nod at.

stages.title: Keep making it better
stages.copy: Change the product because of how it is used. Not because the next slide said so.

sections.heading: Founder-led, on purpose.
paragraphs: Player29 was started by product manager Oliver Kyte to make digital products he would actually want to use.
Strategy, design and software sit together. When a product needs a specialist — in design, engineering, or something more particular — we bring in people we trust.
That keeps the important calls close to the making of the thing, and the team the right size for the product in front of us.

sections.heading: Got a strong idea, a format, or an audience that deserves better?
sections.supporting: Let’s see what it could become — and whether it has another season in it.

contact.heading: Let's talk
